newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA puts $130 million into entertainment.
newsitem.headline: SIA puts $130 million into entertainment.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) is spending some US$130 million to retrofit more than half its fleet with a new inflight entertainment system and expects to experiment with onboard gaming by the end of the year.

Thirty-seven Boeing 747-400 aircraft are expected to be retrofitted with the KrisWorld inflight entertainment system at at average cost of $3.5 million each by the middle of next year, Director of marketing services, Tjhoen Onn Thoeng, said on Wednesday.
Theong told Reuters that newer aircraft, like the four Airbus A340s recently delivered, will come fitted with the entertainment system, developed for SIA by Matsushita.
The system, which currently offers several video and music channels, Nintendo games and Reuters news service to all passengers, will be expanded to allow gaming on board the aircraft by next year.
Thoeng said SIA aims to start the trial run for inflight gaming despite an American law that bans gambling on flights to and from the United States.
"The service would be introduced on some Southeast Asian and also European flights initially. It will only be available on longer-haul flights of three hours and above," Thoeng said.
He said the inflight gaming software, which includes blackjack and poker, will limit losses to $350 and wins to $3,500.
"It is meant to be a form of entertainment and not meant for us to make money," he said.
Thoeng said planned enhancements to KrisWorld include audio and video on demand in the first and business class sections of the aircraft by next year, and possibly the Internet at a later stage.
